news.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president apologises for World Cup sell-off plan - but FA and other European leaders still want him to resign
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan at a three-hour FIFA Council meeting in Zurich on Thursday. His expression of regret for not telling the council about his plans earlier was not good enough for European football leaders, including FA chair Debbie Hewitt, who still want him to resign. UEFA want Infantino to release all documents relating to the plan as they believe the 20 per cent stake in all future FIFA tournaments was being sold for a knockdown price. Infantino abandons plans to sell off stake in World Cup Pressure to resign increases on Infantino with news he received £1.3m in 2024 It was expected council members would also quiz Infantino on a number of controversial issues at the meeting.

news.title: FIFA meeting: Infantino apologises over World Cup row but fails to win over critics
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologised to members of the governing body's council on Thursday over his handling of a proposed USD 4.2 billion investment deal but failed to provide the documents and answers sought by European football officials. The proposal, introduced in July and later abandoned, would have given private investors a stake in a subsidiary managing the commercial rights to the World Cup and Club World Cup. Its withdrawal did little to ease tensions within FIFA, with UEFA continuing to challenge Infantino's leadership ahead of the presidential election in March. Infantino also faced questions over the red-card case involving United States forward Folarin Balogun at the World Cup and US President Donald Trump's reported intervention in support of the player.

news.title: Spain includes Bernabeu, Camp Nou among venues in 2035 World Cup bid
news.lede: Soccer Football - LaLiga - FC Barcelona v Getafe - Spotify Camp Nou, Barcelona, Spain - October 10, 2026 General view inside the stadium before the match REUTERS/Albert Gea. Oct 15 - Spain has put forward some of the country's biggest football stadiums, including Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu and Barcelona's Camp Nou, as part of its bid to host the 2035 Rugby World Cup, the Spanish Rugby Federation said on Wednesday. The RFER submitted its detailed applicant questionnaire to World Rugby this month and has now unveiled a list of potential venues that also includes Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium, as Spain seeks to host the event for the first time. Backed by LaLiga, the bid plans to capitalise on infrastructure developed for the 2030 football World Cup, which Spain will co-host with Portugal and Morocco.

news.title: At Showdown FIFA Meeting, Infantino Apologizes For World Cup Furor But Leaves Critics Unhappy
news.lede: Zurich: Gianni Infantino gave an apology to his toughest critics but no new details or documents on FIFA issues that most concern them at a showdown meeting of its ruling council Thursday. No documents about the $4.2 billion World Cup sell-off plan he launched and dropped in July. No details about the Folarin Balogun red-card case at the World Cup and how U.S. President Donald Trump intervened to help the national team forward.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa president apologises over World Cup move but told he must do more
news.lede: Gianni Infantino celebrated 10 years as Fifa president in February 2026. President Gianni Infantino has apologised to the Fifa Council for his World Cup sell-off plan - but has been told he is not fit to lead unless he releases all of the documents and answers key questions. The Fifa Council met in Zurich on Thursday for the first time since Infantino's secret Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal emerged. Under FFE, which Infantino scrapped within days, a portion of the commercial rights of football's world governing body would have been given to a private investment firm.
